subject: Discovery recap: Data privacy & logging requirements
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@healthsys.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 08 Oct 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: Data privacy & logging requirements

Hi Alex / Emily,

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and next steps so we have alignment. I've captured the key pain points, success criteria, and questions we agreed to follow up on.

Pain points / background
- You're running multiple patient-facing services across web and mobile that ingest PHI and need strict controls around what gets logged and stored.
- Current stack: in-house API gateway -> downstream ML features (NLP for triage) -> long-term archival in S3.
- Primary concerns: PII/PHI redaction, retention limits, auditability of who/what was sent to model endpoints, and customer-managed encryption keys for any persisted artifacts.

Success criteria for a pilot (what would make this successful):
- Ability to prevent storage of raw PHI for specified routes (disable logging or automatic redaction).
- Retention configurable per-customer and per-endpoint (example target: 90 days or less for session data; ability to zero-retain logs for some endpoints).
- Provide verifiable audit logs showing event timestamps, request metadata, and redaction status (not full raw content unless customer allows).
- Support for customer-managed keys (CMEK) or HSM for at-rest encryption of any persisted artifacts.
- SOC 2 / HIPAA evidence and a clear mutual action plan for a 4\u20136 week pilot.

Open questions we'll follow up on
- Which endpoints do you want to be no-log vs redact-by-default? (Emily / Alex to list)
- Do you require CMEK for the pilot or is a dedicated, encrypted instance acceptable as a first step?
- Expected volume for pilot (rps and token-volume) so we can size Dedicated vs Private.

Next steps
1) I'll send over a short capabilities one-pager and our SOC 2 summary (attached).
2) Dev will follow up with technical details on redaction options and log export / retention capabilities.
3) Schedule an SE deep-dive next week to review architecture and produce a mutual action plan.

Attachments: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf, redwood-privacy-capabilities-one-pager.pdf

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@healthsys.com>

Date: Thu, 08 Oct 2026 17:09:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Data privacy & logging requirements

Marissa,

Thanks for the clear recap. This aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side: we're a regulated healthcare provider, so PHI handling is the top constraint. A couple items to call out:

- Retention: legal has historically required very long retention for audit trails (up to 7 years for some record types), but for the ML request payloads we want the option to keep only metadata and hashes while expiring raw content quickly (90 days is our preferred upper bound for raw session content).
- CMEK: we prefer CMEK for any persisted artifacts; if that's not immediately possible for hosted offerings, we'd like it for Dedicated/Private pilot.
- Audit logs: we need exportable audit logs (preferably in a format we can ingest to Splunk/Elastic) and a clear tamper-evidence model.
- Redaction: ML-based PII detection is desirable, but we also need deterministic controls (regex, field-blocklist) for particular routes.

I've attached our security questionnaire so you can see the level of detail procurement will expect. Happy to get the SE call scheduled. Emily and I are available next Tue/Wed afternoon PT.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Johnson
Director of Product, HealthSys Medical
alex.johnson@healthsys.com

Attachment: healthsys-security-questionnaire.pdf

Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Data privacy & logging requirements

Alex / Emily,

Appreciate the context. Quick technical summary / answers to the items you raised:

1) Logging & no-log routes
- Redwood supports per-route logging policies. For Hosted API, you can mark routes as "no-persist" so request/response bodies are not written to long-term storage; only minimal metadata (timestamps, status, token counts) are kept for operational monitoring. For Dedicated and Private deployments we can fully disable persistence for specific endpoints.

2) Redaction options
- Two layers available: a) deterministic rules (field blocklist, regex-based masks) and b) ML PII detectors (NER-based redaction with confidence thresholds).
- Redaction can be applied client-side (SDK middleware) or server-side in the inference path. We recommend server-side for guaranteed enforcement.

3) Retention & export
- Retention is configurable per-customer and per-channel. Minimum retention for logs can be set to 0 days for immediate expiry; typical pilot configuration we suggest: raw payloads 90 days, metadata 365 days.
- Audit logs are exportable to S3, GCS, or streamed to SIEMs (Splunk/Elastic) via our log-forwarder. Exports include an integrity hash and event sequence to help with tamper detection.

4) Encryption / CMEK
- CMEK/HSM support is available for Private deployments and Dedicated (enterprise tier). Hosted customers get AES-256 at rest but not CMEK unless we provision a private tenancy. We can scope a Dedicated pilot with CMEK to meet your requirement.

5) Evidence / compliance docs
- We can provide SOC 2 Type II summary and our SOC auditor contact. For HIPAA, we offer a BAA for Dedicated/Private customers; I'll surface the standard BAA template for review.

Next steps (technical)
- I've proposed a 60-min technical deep-dive to review your routes and map redaction/no-log policies. Please pick a slot: https://calendly.com/redwood-se/healthsys-technical-deep-dive
- I'll prepare an example retention matrix and a sample export (CSV/JSON) of audit events for review.

If helpful, I can also produce a short architecture sketch showing how CRM -> Redwood inference -> archival works with CMEK and log-forwarding.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
